name: Saccular Limited Dorsal Myeloschisis
aliases: Limited Dorsal Myeloschisis with Saccular Lesion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Limited Dorsal Myeloschisis

criteria.description: Presence of a midline saccular skin lesion overlying the spinal cord
Identification of a fibroneural stalk connecting the skin lesion to the underlying spinal cord on MRI
Histopathological confirmation of absence of neural tissue within the sac
Presence of neurological deficits consistent with spinal cord tethering

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of a midline saccular lesion with MRI evidence of a fibroneural stalk connecting the lesion to the spinal cord
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by MRI findings; histopathology is confirmatory but not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Midline saccular cutaneous lesion over spinal axis
searchTerms: skin sac-like lesion on spine midline

pathognomonic.symptomName: Fibroneural stalk connecting skin lesion to spinal cord
searchTerms: fibrous tissue connecting skin lesion to spinal cord
stalk linking skin cyst to spinal cord
skin lesion attached to spinal cord by stalk

common.symptomName: Cutaneous stigmata such as hypertrichosis or dermal sinus
searchTerms: skin signs like excess hair or skin pits
cutaneous markers such as hairy patches or sinuses
sensory loss in feet and legs

occasional.symptomName: Back pain localized to lesion site

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus secondary to associated neural tube defects
searchTerms: fluid buildup in brain due to neural tube defects
brain fluid accumulation secondary to spinal problems
infection of skin near lower spine

imaging: MRI demonstrating fibroneural stalk connecting saccular lesion to spinal cord
Ultrasound may show cystic lesion in neonates
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; considered a neural tube closure defect
other: Histopathology showing absence of neural tissue within sac and presence of fibroneural stalk

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of neural tissue within the sac

redFlags: Signs of spinal cord tethering with worsening motor or bladder function
Infection or leakage from the sac
references: Pang D, et al. Limited dorsal myeloschisis: a distinctive clinicopathological entity. Neurosurgery. 2010.
Radiological features of limited dorsal myeloschisis: MRI correlation. J Neurosurg Pediatr. 2015.
